A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeltaProduct and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. The retained material and substantive revisions can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v5 reports original state-tracking, formal-language, language-modeling, and runtime experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v7 retains original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix C and reports revised throughput comparisons.

M1.justification: v7 introduces a theoretical variant replacing Householder factors with RWKV-7 transition matrices (Section B.4, Equation 6). This changes the recurrence's components, but the central DeltaProduct method remains unchanged, and the variant is not experimentally evaluated.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same permutation groups, parity and modular-arithmetic tasks, FineWeb training data, language-modeling benchmarks, and extrapolation datasets. The new regular-language theorem does not add empirically evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2–5 are retained, as is DeltaNet in the throughput comparisons. The new RWKV-7-product construction is theoretical rather than an added empirical baseline.

E3.justification: The efficiency evaluations change to parameter-matched 1.3B models using head count, head dimension, or SwiGLU width adjustments. Figures 4 and 14 now sweep n_h=1–3 instead of 1–4, and the earlier 340M inference-latency evaluation is removed. Benchmark training and evaluation protocols are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: The revised throughput analyses examine how different parameter-matching strategies affect the computational cost of increasing n_h. The existing depth/eigenvalue sweeps, key-vector PCA, hidden-state-rank analyses, and language-model scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs with different seeds and select the best result for the formal-language experiments (Section C.2, Table 2). No new uncertainty-reporting practices, run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 14 contain replacement throughput results under revised configurations; the 340M inference-latency results disappear. Section 5.1 newly reports a 20% faster forward pass for an optimized kernel relative to DeltaNet's kernel. Tables 2–5 and the retained state-tracking and extrapolation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: v7 adds a decoder-injectivity lemma and proof in B.1.1 and a regular-language expressivity theorem for RWKV-7 products in B.4. Appendix A replaces an implicit spectral threshold with explicit coefficient/angle bounds and revised reasoning. It also corrects the RMSNorm formula, word-product definitions, and several proof expressions, substantially extending and refining the theoretical material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about Householder products, expressivity controlled by n_h, and improved state-tracking, language modeling, and length extrapolation.

C2.justification: v7 develops the stability–expressivity tradeoff for RWKV-7 products, clarifies problem-dependent MLP width and RMSNorm information bottlenecks, and explains throughput penalties from head-dimension padding. Section B.6 also removes the blanket assertion that instability causes exponentially fast divergence.

D1.justification: v7 adds information about the optimized Triton kernel and parameter matching, including SwiGLU inner-width adjustment. Section 4 replaces the explicit sigmoid-gate formula with a Mamba2-derived scalar-gate description; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Core training hyperparameters, GPU types, and code-access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v7 adds Nerode's 1958 work on linear automaton transformations and extends its theoretical positioning relative to RWKV-7. It also removes the claimed similarity between observed low hidden-state ranks and Parnichkun et al., while retaining that citation and the broader related-work discussion.

P1.justification: The revision makes local language corrections and expands several proof explanations, especially the decoder and dihedral-group discussions. A new B.4 subsection shifts the existing dihedral and stability subsections, while the overall main-text and appendix organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 4 becomes a two-panel parameter-matched throughput comparison, and Figure 14 replaces its throughput/latency pair with one throughput panel. Several retained figures and tables are relocated, and the publication header and page layout are updated.

improvement.justification: The explicit spectral bounds and decoder-injectivity proof make previously less-developed arguments more checkable, while parameter matching improves the efficiency comparison. These gains outweigh the limited loss of evidence from removing the 340M inference-latency plot. The central contributions and benchmark findings remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
